title: Hosted API: micro-floor + usage-weighted IO rephasing pilot
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a pricing pilot that tests a low-value per-account micro-floor combined with a usage-weighted rephasing of ingress/egress (input/output) rates to reduce bill shock for streaming-heavy customers and preserve unit economics. This ticket defines variants, cohorts, metrics, and rollout gating for an initial 6-week field trial with 120 customers.
experiment_design: Objective: validate whether a micro-floor (small monthly minimum charge ~ $5-15) plus smoothing of IO split over billing windows improves revenue predictability, reduces committed-billing friction, and lowers customer support tickets related to variable streaming spikes.

Cohorts: random assignment of eligible self-serve customers (n ~ 120), stratified by monthly token volume: low (<50k), mid (50k-500k), high (>500k); exclude customers on Dedicated/Private contracts and those with active enterprise negotiations.

Variants: control (existing per-token ingress/egress rates + current streaming billing), V1 micro-floor only, V2 usage-rephasing only (smooth per-direction IO split across billing windows with grace credits), V3 micro-floor + rephasing combined.
Experiment length: 6 weeks active + 2 weeks burn-in and 2 weeks observation after variant end.

Billing implementation note: micro-floor applies as credit if gross bill < floor, visible as 'floor adjustment' line item; rephasing uses rolling 7-day normalized IO split for streaming tokens when calculating directional rates.

Exclusions & safeguards: automatic opt-out if variance in daily token spend > 3x baseline for 3 consecutive days; early rollback safety if estimated unit cost to Redwood increases > 15% for any cohort.
Security/Compliance: no billing metadata exposes raw prompt or response content; all experiments must pass legal review per security_review_required.
Data retention: experiment telemetry retained for 12 months; aggregated metrics only used in reports.
metrics: Primary: net revenue delta (delta ARR uplift from micro-floor minus any churn) — target: +8% net revenue from pilot cohorts
Primary: customer support ticket volume related to unexpected billing — target: -25% relative to control
Secondary: churn rate during trial window — target: no increase vs baseline
Secondary: average effective per-token realized price (by direction) and variance — target: variance reduction >= 20%
Operational: number of automated rollbacks triggered, and number of manual interventions — target: zero rollbacks for high cohort
Safety: unit cost delta to Redwood (cost per token after routing/fallback) — must remain < +10% for any cohort
Qualitative: customer sentiment from post-trial survey (CSAT/NPS question) — target: net positive sentiment change
acceptance_criteria: Experiment code deployed to billing-sandbox and passes end-to-end verification with synthetic workloads
Dashboard with cohort-level metrics (revenue, support tickets, churn, unit cost) available and validated by Finance and Observability teams
Legal sign-off on micro-floor contract language and visibility in invoices
Security review completed and documented (security_review_required = true)
Pilot data demonstrates either revenue-safe improvement (meeting primary revenue + safety targets) or clear rollback triggers identified and mitigations planned
linked_artifacts: GitHub: repo/billing-service PR#948 - implement micro-floor invoice line
rollout_plan: Phase 0: sandbox validation and finance sim (2 weeks)
Phase 1: limited pilot (first 4 weeks) with 30 customers across strata — monitor daily
Phase 2: scale to full cohort (weeks 5-6) if no safety triggers
Phase 3: analysis and decision (week 8) — promote to wider product if criteria met or iterate on pricing bands
Rollback plan: immediate rollback to control for a cohort if unit cost delta > 15% or if billing complaints exceed threshold
data_analysis_plan: Precompute baseline monthly and 7-day rolling IO splits per customer for previous 90 days
Measure delta in realized customer bill vs synthetic expected bill under control and variants
Attribution: isolate changes due to streaming spikes by analyzing per-minute token ingress/egress histograms
Statistical significance: require p < 0.05 for primary revenue metric with power 0.8
Post-hoc segments: identify customer archetypes (chat-first, ingestion-heavy, embeddings-heavy) and report differential impacts
